mechanism_narrative: People in Tokyo have adapted to a reduced level of retail and recreation activity, and without a significant external shock or policy change, this suppressed mobility will persist over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rebound in workplace attendance, indicated by WORKPLACES rising above -15% from baseline, will drive increased weekday foot traffic to retail and recreation venues, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -15% from baseline, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If residential time spent at home decreases significantly while transit usage simultaneously increases, it signals a broader shift towards out-of-home activities, which will boost retail and recreation mobility within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 7% AND TRANSIT rises above -20%
failure_condition: Both RESIDENTIAL falls below 7% and TRANSIT rises above -20%, yet RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in parks visitation, especially after a period of low activity, suggests a general willingness for outdoor leisure that can spill over into nearby retail and recreation within a week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high levels of residential mobility indicate a continued preference for staying home, which directly suppresses out-of-home activities like retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL remains above 7% on average, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in transit station visits, indicated by TRANSIT rising above -20% from baseline for two consecutive weeks, will facilitate increased access to and engagement with retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -20% from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -20% for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If both workplace attendance and essential grocery/pharmacy visits increase, it suggests a broader return to out-of-home routines, creating opportunities for incidental retail and recreation engagement over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -18% AND GROCERY_PHARM rises above -13%
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES rises above -18% and GROCERY_PHARM rises above -13%, yet RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If RETAIL_REC averages consistently below -20% over the last four weeks, it indicates persistent underlying constraints or strong behavioral shifts that will continue to suppress activity in the near term, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC averages below -20% over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages below -20% over the last four weeks, but RETAIL_REC increases in the subsequent two weeks.
